key_insight: GLoC-EHR improves clinical question answering by combining global trajectory context with local EHR evidence and training the model to cite record-supported reasons before answering.
clinical_relevance: This approach may make EHR-based predictions more reliable and more interpretable by linking answers to specific patient events rather than only generating a final prediction.
method: Builds two memories from structured EHRs: a fixed-size global memory for the full course and a local memory for selected events.
Pretrains with multitask objectives to generate hospital-course summaries and masked concept descriptions aligned to clinical text.
Uses rationale fine-tuning plus GRPO to reward both correct answers and evidence supported by the record.
evidence_signal: On three MIMIC-IV outcome tasks, it achieved the best macro AUROC among compared models in direct answering, stayed close to that performance with evidence-cited reasoning, and transferred to EHRSHOT on par with EHR-BERT.
watch_item: Evidence-cited reasoning improved support quality, but the gains depended on task setting and the model still requires careful validation before real-world deployment.
paper_title: GLoC-EHR: Evidence-Cited Clinical Reasoning over Global Context and Local EHR Events
